caption:
Mr Turtle booked a chiro visit, but that crack sound makes him nervous. The sound is usually a gas bubble. Joints sit in a pocket of fluid, and when a joint is stretched quickly, pressure drops and a bubble forms. That rapid change is widely thought to make the pop.

It doesn't mean a bone was out of place and has been put back. Some adjustments are silent, and research suggests the sound isn't what makes treatment feel helpful. How you move afterwards matters more.

Not keen on being adjusted? Just say so. Our chiropractors combine hands-on care with exercise and advice, and gentler options are always available. Book online via the link in bio 🐢

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
